companies.latest_signal: Core Local Commerce swung back to a RMB5.7bn profit (7.9% margin) in Q2 2026 from a Q1 2026 loss, with delivery revenue returning to positive YoY growth for the first time since the war began as management described 'prudent' (审慎) incentive spending rather than matching rivals.

companies.label: Alibaba
companies.metric_basis: Alibaba does not disclose a standalone Taobao Flash Sale/Ele.me loss line; the closest company-disclosed proxy is the 'China E-commerce Group' segment Adjusted EBITA (bundles Taobao/Tmall core profit against instant-commerce investment), reported in HKEX/SEC filings
companies.latest_signal: The blended e-commerce EBITA nearly matched year-ago levels in the June 2026 quarter (-1% YoY vs -76% at the Sept 2025 trough), with management citing sequential unit-economics improvement at Taobao Instant Commerce; but sell-side estimates (中金/Morgan Stanley, via 21jingji/Jiemian) still put the standalone Flash Sale/Ele.me EBITA loss around RMB17-19bn in Q1 2026, so group-level recovery partly reflects core Taobao/Tmall re-acceleration rather than proof the instant-commerce P&L itself is near breakeven.

companies.latest_signal: New Businesses loss fell to RMB9.9bn in Q2 2026 from RMB14.8bn a year earlier as JD Food Delivery's loss more than halved YoY on tighter ROI discipline, though comparability is clouded since on-demand delivery revenue recognition shifted to JD Logistics starting Q1 2026.

war_summary: Subsidy intensity peaked around Q3 2025 (Goldman estimated combined 12-month losses of roughly RMB41bn for Alibaba's delivery push, RMB26bn for JD and a RMB25bn EBIT hit for Meituan) before SAMR intervened directly: a March 2026 'the delivery war should end' signal, May and July 2026 summons of Meituan, Ele.me and JD, and a June 2026 ten-point subsidy code all three platforms publicly endorsed. By Q2 2026 each reported narrowing on its own disclosed proxy — Meituan's core local commerce flipped back to a RMB5.7bn profit, Alibaba's e-commerce group EBITA nearly matched year-ago levels, and JD's new-business loss roughly halved YoY. JD blinked first, capping delivery share near 15% rather than chasing parity, while Meituan defended share and Alibaba still carries the largest (undisclosed but analyst-estimated) standalone instant-commerce loss.
